State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Ram Ishwar Yadav vs State Bank Of India on 7 April, 2022
ADDITIONAL BENCH

STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
 PUNJAB, CHANDIGARH.

 First Appeal No.618 of 2019
 Date of institution : 18.09.2019
 Reserved on : 28.03.2022
 Date of decision : 07.04.2022

Ram Ishwar Yadav son of Sh. Kanhaiya Yadav, R/o H.No.94, Gobind
Nagar, Railway Station Road, Malerkotla, Tehsil Malerkotla, District
Sangrur.
 .....Appellant/Complainant
 Versus

State Bank of India, Branch Office : College Road, Malerkotla, Tehsil
Malerkotla, District Sangrur, through its Branch Manager-148023.

 ....Respondent/Opposite Party

 First Appeal under
Section 15
the
 Consumer Protection Act, against the order
 dated 31.05.2019 of the District Consumer
 Disputes Redressal Forum (now
 'Commission'), Sangrur.
Quorum:-
 Mr. Rajinder Kumar Goyal, Presiding Member
Mrs. Kiran Sibal, Member

Present:-
For the appellant : Sh. Pardeep Singh, Advocate
 For respondent : None

KIRAN SIBAL, MEMBER

 The instant appeal has been filed by the
appellant/complainant against the order dated 31.05.2019 passed by

District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Sangrur (in short, now

"the District Commission"), whereby the complaint filed by complainant
FA No.618 of 2019 2
against opposite party (in short 'OP'), under the
Consumer Protection

Act, 1986
, was dismissed. The relevant portion of the impugned order

is reproduced as under:-
"6........... As proceedings before the Consumer Forum

 are summary in nature, but allegations of forgery

 leveled in this case requires elaborate evidence and as

 such, complainant, if advised may approach the Civil

 Court of competent jurisdiction because complex

 question of law and facts qua fraud can be decided by

 that Court and not in these summary proceedings".
2. It would be apposite to mention that hereinafter the parties

will be referred, as have been arrayed before the District Commission.
3. Brief facts for the disposal of the appeal are that the

complainant was having a saving bank account No.31162067573 with

OP Bank and had been availing ATM Card facility and on every

transaction, message was being sent on the registered mobile

No.98144-84053 of the complainant. On 25.10.2017, an unidentified

and unknown person fraudulently exchanged the ATM card from the

son of the complainant in ATM House situated at Truck Union, Near

Kewal Shiv Mandir, Malerkotla. The ATM card, which was fraudulently

handed over to the son of the complainant, was in the name of one

Kalyan Singh Rajput of Udaipur. The said unidentified person, in

connivance with the officials of OP, just to usurp huge amount and to

play fraud upon the complainant, first stopped message service on the

registered mobile phone of the complainant and thereafter withdrew
FA No.618 of 2019 3
the total amount of Rs.2,77,902/- on various dates and misutilized the

same. The complainant was unaware about the said transactions as

no message was sent on the registered mobile phone of the

complainant by the OP. The complainant came to know about the said

illegal transactions on 14.11.2017 when he went to ATM for withdrawal

of amount. He approached OP, who assured the complainant that

whole amount would be reversed. But OP did not initiate any action in

the said matter. Therefore, the complainant lodged an FIR No.121

dated 24.11.2017 under
Section 420
IPC, at P.S.City-1, Malerkotla

against unknown person, but nothing was recovered. Alleging

deficiency in service on the part of the OP, the complainant filed the

consumer complaint before the District Commission and sought refund

of Rs.2,77,902/- along with interest @18% p.a. and compensation to

the tune of Rs.50,000/- on account of mental tension, agony and

physical harassment and Rs.11,000/- as litigation expenses.
4. The complaint was contested by the OP, who filed written

reply before the District Commission. In its written reply, OP raised

certain legal objections, inter alia, that the complainant has alleged the

commission of fraud and cheating with him by fraudster and lodged

FIR under
section 420
IPC before the policy authorities, therefore, the

complaint was not maintainable before District Commission. The

complainant was negligent as well as was responsible in regard to

operation of his account as his son had shared the Card Credentials

with fraudster person standing in the ATM room, beside handing over

the ATM card to him and sharing the secret PIN code to withdraw the
FA No.618 of 2019 4
amount of Rs.10,000/-. As such, the complainant had no locus standi

to file the complaint and the complaint was bad for non joinder of

necessary parties. On merits, OP stated that as regard the receipt of

messages regarding withdrawal through ATM card is concerned, the

messages are not sent by the OP. The SMS is generated and

delivered to the customer's registered mobile numbers by the SMS

INFRONICS Team, who informed the OP that there was no log found

for the disputed transactions. No CCTV footage had been provided to

the OP by the outsourced agencies. There was no deficiency in

service on the part of the OP. After denying the other averments made

in the complaint, OP prayed for dismissal of the complaint.
5. Parties led their evidence in support of their respective

contentions before the District Commission and after hearing the

learned counsel for the parties, the complaint was dismissed vide

impugned order dated 31.05.2019 as above. Aggrieved by the said

order, this appeal has been filed by the appellant/complainant for

setting aside the same.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and have

also gone through written submission filed by parties as well as record

of the case.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant, vehemently contended

that the District Commission wrongly and illegally dismissed the

complaint of the appellant/complainant on the ground that allegations

of forgery have been leveled in the complaint but it failed to appreciate
FA No.618 of 2019 5
the fact that there is also negligence on the part of the respondent

Bank. The District Commission further failed to appreciate the fact that

the appellant/complainant lost his amount due to non sending of

messages by the respondent/OP bank. The respondent/OP bank has

received charges from appellant/complainant for sending of messages

to him but it has stopped sending the messages without giving any

information or reason for the same. The appellant was unaware about

the withdrawals by the said person as no message was sent to him by

the respondent/OP Bank on his registered mobile number. The

learned counsel further contended that RBI has issued guidelines

dated 06.07.2017 regarding Zero liability of a customer. The relevant

portion of the said guideline is reproduced as under:-
(a) Zero Liability of a Customer
6. A customer's entitlement to zero liability shall arise where the
 unauthorised transaction occurs in the following events:
(i) Contributory fraud/ negligence/ deficiency on the part of the
 bank (irrespective of whether or not the transaction is reported
 by the customer).
(ii) Third party breach where the deficiency lies neither with
 the bank nor with the customer but lies elsewhere in the system,
 and the customer notifies the bank within three working days
 of receiving the communication from the bank regarding the
 unauthorised transaction.
Alleging negligence and deficiency in service on the part of the

respondent/OP, the learned counsel prayed for acceptance of the

present appeal and setting aside of the impugned order.
8. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the

respondent/OP contended that the District Commission has rightly

dismissed the complaint filed before it as the complainant had alleged

the commission of fraud and cheating with him. The learned counsel
FA No.618 of 2019 6
further contended that the ATM card facility was provided only to the

appellant/complainant and as per banking norms, the person other

than the ATM card holder is not legally entitled to operate the ATM

Card, even with the permission of the ATM card holder. The card

holder is bound to keep the PIN number confidential. Admittedly, the

appellant/complainant handed over the ATM card and disclosed the

four digit PIN number to his son and allowed him to use the same and

his son further handed over the ATM card to a stranger, who withdrew

the money fraudulently. The alleged fraudulent withdrawals occurred

as the ATM and its Pin Number fell in wrong hands due to the

negligence on the part of the appellant/complainant. There is no

negligence and deficiency in service on the part of the respondent/ OP

bank. The learned counsel prayed for dismissal of the present appeal.
9. We have given thoughtful consideration to the contentions

raised by the parties.
10. The admitted facts of the case are that the

appellant/complainant is having his saving bank account with the OP

bank and an amount of Rs.2,77,902/- has been withdrawn/transferred

by unidentified person through the ATM Card of the complainant. The

complainant approached the OP bank but they failed to redress the

grievance of the complainant. Therefore, the complainant filed a

Consumer Complaint before the District Commission, which was

dismissed, vide impugned order reproduced as above. The grievance

of the appellant/complainant is that the District Commission, instead of

appreciating the fact of negligence on the part of the OP Bank, has
FA No.618 of 2019 7
dismissed the complaint of the complainant without going into merits of

the case on the ground that fraud and forgery needs voluminous

evidence therefore the complaint was not maintainable.
11. The foremost point for consideration before us is whether

the District Commission has rightly dismissed the complaint on the

ground of forgery or not? A perusal of the complaint and perusal of

affidavit of the complainant, Ex. C-1, shows that allegations made in

the complaint are with regard to unauthorized use of ATM card by a

third person, who had withdrawn an amount of Rs.2,77,902/- on

various dates through ATM withdrawal, online purchase and transfer to

another account. The appellant/complainant, being a consumer of the

respondent/OP Bank, also leveled allegations that due to non-sending

of messages by the bank on his mobile number he suffered the said

loss. The District Commission, while passing the impugned order,

relied on the Judgment of Hon'ble National Commission, in case titled

Bright Transport Company Versus Sangli Sahakari Bank Limited

reported in II (2012) CPJ-151 (NC), wherein it was held that the

complaints which are based on allegations of fraud, forgery etc and

trial of which would require voluminous evidence and consideration are

not to be entertained by the Consumer Commission. But the authority

relied upon by the District Commission is not applicable to the facts of

the present case, as the facts of that case are distinguishable from the

present case. In the cited authority the amount was encashed by

putting forged signatures on the cheque, but in the present case, the

amount was withdrawn by exchanging the ATM card of the

complainant by a third person illegally. Therefore, we do not agree
FA No.618 of 2019 8
with the finding of the District Commission that Consumer

Commissions have no jurisdiction to decide the present case.
12. This matter is no more res-integra. The Hon'ble Supreme

Court in case "
Dr. J.J. Merchant & Ors. v. Shrinath Chaturvedi
",

2002 (2)
CPC
-640, held that "under the Act, the Hon'ble National

Commission is headed by a retired Judge of the Hon'ble Supreme

Court and the State Commission is headed by a retired High Court

Judge. Similarly, the District Forums are headed by retired

District/Additional Session Judge or the person of legal background

having equivalent experience and, as such, they are competent to

decide the complicated issues of law or facts. It is expected of them to

decide the cases on merits, on the basis of prima facie evidence on

the record."
Similarly, in
Shiv Kumar Agarwal v. Arun Tonden &

Anr.
, 2007 (2)
CPC
129 (NC), it was observed by the Hon'ble National

Commission in Para No.5, which is reproduced below:-
5. We heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner and
 perused the material on record. Like before the State
 Commission, the learned Counsel for the petitioner argued
 before us that this case involves complicated questions of fact
 and law and will need expert evidence, which is not possible
 in the summary procedure adopted by the Consumer Fora.
After seeing the complaint, written version as also the
 judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of
Dr.
 J.J. Merchant and Ors. v. Shrinath Chaturvedi
, and other
 catena of judgments, we are of the view that Consumer
 Forum, which is headed by Senior Judicial Officers, are
 capable of dealing with even complex questions.
The
 Consumer Protection Act, 1986
under
Section 13
provides for
 calling for expert evidence, if necessary.
13.
In view of the ratio of law
laid down in
the authority

discussed above, the Consume Fora , now "Consumer Commissions"
are being presided by the competent senior judicial authorities and
FA No.618 of 2019 9
they are capable of dealing with even complex questions of law.

Accordingly, the order of dismissal of the complaint on the ground that

allegations of forgery have been leveled for which elaborate evidence

is required to be led before the Civil Court, is set aside.
14. Now, coming to the merits of the case, the only question

arises for adjudication before us is that whether there is any

fault/negligence on the part of the OP Bank or not? To determine this

controversy, we have perused the entire evidence and pleadings on

record. From the perusal of complaint filed by the complainant as well

as his affidavit Ex.C-1 and even the FIR, Ex. C-2, it clearly shows that

the appellant/complainant himself handed over the ATM card to his

son for using the same and disclosed the four digit PIN number to him.

Furthermore, admittedly his son, handed over the said ATM card to a

stranger/third party and also disclosed the PIN number to him.

Resultantly, the said unknown person cleverly exchanged the ATM

card from the son of the complainant, who was about 28 years old,

and withdrew the alleged amount on different dates through different

modes. Moreover, in the "SBI Debit Card User Guide" placed on

record by respondent/OP Bank as Ex. OP/1, it has been specifically

mentioned as under:-
• Please keep the PIN secret and do not disclose the PIN to
 anybody including your family members and close
 relatives.
• Giving your card and disclosing PIN to someone is like
 giving a blank signed cheque.
• Please refrain from taking help from any stranger while
 doing ATM transaction.
FA No.618 of 2019 10
Accordingly, as per Banking norms, the ATM card holder is bound to

keep the PIN number confidential. Nowadays, banks in India have

been incessantly warning people against scamsters, urging customers

to never share their banking details, ATM pin details, credit card

numbers etc. Despite these warnings, if customers still fail to adhere to

the basic precautionary norms and fall prey to fraudulent schemes or

activities, they will not be able to hold the banks responsible for it.

Further, reliance is placed upon the Circular DBR.No.Leg.BC.

78/09.07.005/2017-18 dated 06.07.2017 issued by the Reserve Bank

of India regarding limiting liability of Customers in Unauthorized

Electric Banking Transactions. The relevant clause is reproduced as

under:-
"Limited Liability of Customer
(a) Zero Liability of a Customer
6. A customer's entitlement to zero liability shall arise where the
 unauthorised transaction occurs in the following events:
(i) Contributory fraud/ negligence/ deficiency on the part of the
 bank (irrespective of whether or not the transaction is reported
 by the customer).
(ii) Third party breach where the deficiency lies neither with
 the bank nor with the customer but lies elsewhere in the system,
 and the customer notifies the bank within three working days
 of receiving the communication from the bank regarding the
 unauthorised transaction.
(b) Limited Liability of a Customer
7. A customer shall be liable for the loss occurring due to
 unauthorised transactions in the following cases:
(i) In cases where the loss is due to negligence by a customer,
 such as where he has shared the payment credentials, the
 customer will bear the entire loss until he reports the
 unauthorised transaction to the bank. Any loss occurring after
 the reporting of the unauthorised transaction shall be borne by
 the bank.
FA No.618 of 2019 11
(ii) In cases where the responsibility for the unauthorised
 electronic banking transaction lies neither with the bank nor
 with the customer, but lies elsewhere in the system and when
 there is a delay (of four to seven working days after receiving
 the communication from the bank) on the RBI,DBR,CO - 4 -
continuation sheet part of the customer in notifying the bank of
 such a transaction, the per transaction liability of the customer
 shall be limited to the transaction value or the amount
 mentioned in Table 1, whichever is lower."
The complainant was duped because of his own negligence, as

discussed above, therefore Clause 7(i) of the above said circular is

applicable that " in cases where the loss is due to negligence by a

customer, such as where he has shared the payment credentials,

the customer will bear the entire loss until he reports the

unauthorised transaction to the bank". The contention of learned

counsel for the appellant/complainant is that if the respondent/OP

Bank had sent the messages regarding the alleged unauthorized

transactions to the appellant, he might be alerted and the remaining

amount could be saved. But to support this contention, nothing has

been placed on record by the appellant/complainant that he is availing

any SMS alert service of the respondent/OP bank with regard to every

transactions made by him. In the absence of any cogent evidence like

printout of previous SMSs or bank statement showing debit entry of

payment for availing such service, it is hard to believe that

appellant/complainant has been availing the said service of the bank.

Accordingly, we do not find any force in the contention raised by the

learned counsel for the appellant/complainant and the same is hereby

rejected. We are of the considered view that there is no deficiency in

service or negligence on the part of respondent/OP bank for the
FA No.618 of 2019 12
alleged loss suffered by the appellant/complainant. Hence, as per

clause 7(i), as discussed above, the liability is of the

appellant/complainant and he shall bear the entire loss as he shared

the payment credentials and there is negligence on his own part.
15. Sequel to our above discussion, we do not find any merit in

the present appeal as well as in the complaint filed before the District

Commission and the same are hereby dismissed with no order as to

costs.
16. The appeal could not be decided within the stipulated

period due to heavy pendency of Court cases and non-sitting of this

Commission due to pandemic of Covid-19.
(RAJINDER KUMAR GOYAL)
 PRESIDING MEMBER

 (KIRAN SIBAL)
 MEMBER

April 7th, 2022.
(Dv)
